comparator.name: Media and Information
comparator.sourceNotes: The first year is common to both specialisations. This comparison shows Cultural Information Studies, the first listed specialisation. The second year includes 36 EC of specialisation courses and 24 EC of common methods and philosophy. Year three includes 42 EC of open electives and the 18 EC research seminar and thesis.
components: The first year also includes an uncredited Academic Literacy Test and tutoring. Tutoring continues in the later years.
Includes academic writing and builds on introductory digital-culture and media study.
Requires positive binding study advice. Analysing Digital Culture and Doing Media Studies 2 are recommended preparation.
Philosophy of the Humanities 2 (Media and Information)
Builds on the first Philosophy of the Humanities course, offered earlier in the semester.
The first Cultural Information Studies course introduces digital humanities research. The guide recommends prior introductory digital culture and media study.
Studies archival principles, practices and their connections to power, identity and institutions.
Builds on Introduction to Digital Humanities and applies Python to cultural data and questions.
Builds on Introduction to Digital Humanities and Coding the Humanities and assumes basic Python.
Free-choice electives, minor, internship or study abroad
The regulations allocate 30 EC of open electives in the first semester and 12 EC in the second. Options include a minor, electives, mobility or a placement, subject to the programme rules.
Research Seminar and Bachelor's Thesis Media and Information
Pass the compulsory first- and second-year courses before entry. Archives, Information and Society is exempt from the entry requirement for this specialisation.

routeSelection.basis: The programme requires a specialisation but the normalized target names neither route. Cultural Information Studies is selected because it is listed first in both the public curriculum and the 2026–27 course catalogue, independently of UCR course availability.

core: Media theory, history and critical analysis of contemporary digital culture
Digital information, platforms, archives and cultural institutions
Digital methods, coding, data analysis and empirical media research
Media-studies research practice, academic argument and independent inquiry
adjacent: Cultural information studies and digital humanities
New media, platform studies and digital cultural practices
Technology, society, identity and digital ethics
questions: How do digital media and information infrastructures shape culture and everyday life?
How can cultural data, archives and online platforms be studied critically and computationally?
How do media technologies transform communication, identity and public knowledge?

alternatives.label: Digital media, culture & information
alternatives.labelReason: The final curriculum balances media theory and cultural analysis with programming, data science, digital methods, communication, sociology and ethics.
alternatives.concept: Study how digital media shape culture and everyday life. Combine film and media analysis, communication and sociology with programming, data analysis and ethical questions about technology.
progression: Programming, media analysis and data preparation precede advanced analytics, media criticism and communication. Machine Learning precedes neural networks.

alternatives.label: Cultural information & digital humanities
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme joins coding and data analysis to archives, museums, literature, history, visual culture and independent humanities research.
alternatives.concept: Study how texts, images and cultural collections are interpreted, organised and shared. Combine art history, museum study and historical research with programming, databases and data analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: 8 courses (60 EC) differ from the closest option in each direction. Art history, museum study and historical inquiry provide a distinct focus for the shared computational methods.
progression: Art history and programming prepare for advanced museum and historical work and data analysis. Data preparation and Machine Learning precede neural networks.

alternatives.label: New media, platforms & digital society
alternatives.labelReason: Media history, digital and public communication, audience research methods and digital strategy support study of platforms in society.
alternatives.concept: Study how media and digital technologies shape public debate, representation and organisations. Combine media analysis, rhetoric and social research with digital strategy and the study of television and online media.
alternatives.distinctness: 60 EC differ from the closest option and 120 EC from cultural information, each way. Rhetoric, social research, platform-era media and digital strategy shift the focus to public communication and organisations.
progression: Introductory film and media, rhetoric and social research prepare for documentary, public communication and media criticism. Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation.

candidates.label: New media, platforms and digital society

blocks: Both develop programming in Python. UCR teaches general computational problem-solving, while UvA applies code to cultural objects and data.
Both collect and analyse digital data. UCR teaches a general R workflow. UvA applies digital methods to media and information research.
Both use concepts to analyse media forms and practices. UCR emphasises film form and media history.
Both examine how media technologies change and shape cultural practice. UCR uses historical objects and infrastructures.
Both develop research design and qualitative interpretation. UCR uses interviews, ethnography and other social-science methods. UvA applies research to media cases.

selection.assessment: Three options address digital media and data, cultural information and historical interpretation, or public communication and digital strategy. Their different course groups support distinct purposes.

notes.text: UCR combines media and cultural study with computing, social research or public communication. UvA provides a dedicated sequence in digital methods, archival studies and coding for the humanities, with an 18 EC research seminar and thesis. Its other specialisation concentrates on new media and digital culture.

audience.programmeDescription: Media and Information at the University of Amsterdam studies how digital media and information shape culture and society. The Cultural Information Studies specialisation focuses on archives, digital humanities and data-driven research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related options in digital media and data, cultural information and historical research, or media and public communication. UvA gives more sustained attention to digital-media research and ends with a required research seminar and thesis.
